Beautiful knives! However, one aspect that doesn't get talked about is how easy they are to sharpen. I bought one of the KAN knives, and it's hardly getting used anymore since I can't sharpen it. Instead the much cheaper Victorinox I can sharpen easily and it's a great kitchen knife. I can't easily find someone trustworthy to sharpen the fancy knives. Not to mention that the sharpening would probably cost like a new Victorinox knife (bought for $24 over 14 years ago, still in great shape). I do have sharpening stones, have watched lots of videos and I have tried sharpening with them but it's not an easy skill to pick up. The Lansky sharpening system works great on the Victorinox steel (X50CrMoV15?) so that's what I use. It doesn't work on the Kan knife (VG-10) though.

Bruhhh 100 year old steel 🥲 There have been so many modern advances in the past couple years with stuff like apex ultra, magnacut, procut, etc. Japan is really way behind the ball in terms of knife steel innovation and trying out new steels, mainly because more modern PM stuff is expensive, and harder to grind. Plus hitachi paper carbon steel is easier to laminate than fancy stainless. This really doesn't sound novel, just because they haven't used a new steel in 30 years doesn't mean a whole lot. God even hitachi paper steel is less than 100 years old. And you can harden steel to whatever you want within a range, a steel in itself isn't "hard", that's not an intrinsic property. Regardless if it is very tough, edge retention will suffer usually, unless you go with one of the more modern super alloys. I don't want to be a downer but for knife nerds a lot of this stuff is hard to watch.

Idk why I'm even commenting this. 

Regardless, I'm a supporter and wish you luck but you won't need it 😉
